lines: The battle with the undead was over, and Revy and I headed to the safehouse we had prepared in advance.
Phew. ...I didn't expect to be dancing all night against those undead.
That was magnificent. If it hadn't been for you, Revy, I don't think we would have made it out.
Well, it felt like I was going on a rampage in a movie. It was fun.
A rampage? Considering that, you were a hundred percent accurate, weren't you?
Huh? Can I take that as a compliment?
...Of course. I'd even like to take lessons from you and the other gunners in our unit.
Heh, I'm passing on the private tutoring offer, but it's not a bad feeling to be praised for my fighting style.
To let the stale air out of the room, I cracked the window open a little, and a faint breeze drifted in from outside.
As the cool morning air rushed in, the lingering scent of battle clinging to us became even more pronounced.
At the smell of rot, gunpowder, and smoke mixed together, Revy grimaced.
We had been splattered with so much blood that it felt more accurate to say we were "cursed" rather than "dirty."
Ah, damn it. Let's wash this off quickly.
Revy roughly pulled off her jacket and headed toward the bathroom.
After the harsh sound of fabric rustling, the sound of the shower began to echo.
This really stinks... the blood of those undead.
Listening to Revy's muttering, I sat down on the sofa and drank some water. I could feel the excitement of the battle fading away.
The sound of the shower continued without pause, and the occasional splashing of water filled the room like a monotonous rain.
I wondered what kind of face Revy was making while bathing. Was it a grim expression, or perhaps a slightly relaxed, vulnerable profile?
Listening to the monotonous sound of water, I started to feel sleepy. My whole body felt so heavy that I might fall asleep if I closed my eyes.
But then, a thud came from the bathroom.
I just stumbled a bit, don't worry about it.
It sounds like her usual quip, but her breathing seems a little ragged.
Recalling how Revy had been during the fight, I decided to suggest a possible cause for her discomfort.
Could it be the effect of the blood splatter? The blood of demons like vampires carries a curse and can be toxic.
I might have been protected by my suit, but... you were exposed directly, Revy.
Tch... It's not that nasty. But yeah, it is a staple in zombie movies.
You'll be fine if you wash it off thoroughly.
Yeah, yeah, I'm already doing it.
Who would've thought a boy like you would fuss over me like a knight in shining armor?
I'm not doing it for that reason. It's only natural to look out for a business partner.
Heh, that's for sure... You're a pain.
But hey... I don't mind that sort of thing.
Her voice, coming through the shower, sounded a bit drained.
Talking to someone like this... it might actually be pretty rare.
Does that mean... you trust me?
Hearing such kind words from someone I respect, my heart raced involuntarily.
Who knows. Trust is only born when you can entrust your back to someone and survive. I just make the call each time.
I could hear the relaxation in Revy's voice. It seemed the poison was being washed away.
Hey, Ninja Boy. What kind of music do you usually listen to?
Yeah. Like when you're taking a shower or after a mission. You're not playing the shakuhachi flute to fit the ninja image, are you?
What kind of image do you have of the shakuhachi?! I'm just talking about the kind of songs that play on a regular streaming service!
What the hell, don't disappoint me like that. I was actually looking forward to you performing on the shamisen.
That's a bit too much to ask.
Revy's light laughter echoed through the room.
Eventually, the sound of the shower stopped, and Revy emerged into the steam-filled air.
Revy, you look a lot better than before.
I feel refreshed. But I still feel like the stench of rot is soaked into my insides.
Well... that's only natural after soaking in all that.
I was using up all the body soap in the bathroom at a furious pace.
Revy let out a sigh, her gaze falling on the table. Resting there was that damned little box.
I thought it was just a plain jewelry box, but it came with a hell of a "bonus."
Who on earth is your client, Revy, to want something so troublesome?
Beats me. It's not my business what perverts want to collect.
If you're going to play at being Van Helsing, you should throw in a silver stake as a service, but I have no obligation to go that far.
Please don't take on jobs that are too suspicious or dangerous. It gives me a heart attack.
It's not about whether it's dangerous, it's about the pay. For me, if the risk is worth the reward, it's justice.
Well, but thanks to teaming up with you this time, we managed to wrap it up, I guess.
...As a partner, I'm still quite inexperienced.
That's just room for growth. I'll train you properly.
You mean train me on the battlefield, right?
What else could it be? Do you want me to put on a triangular monocle and be your tutor?
Alright, once we deliver this, it's celebration time. I'm buying you a drink.
Idiot, there's no such thing as morning or night for this kind of thing.
...I suppose so. In that case, I'll join you. But do you have any specific places in mind?
Of course not. But if you just wander around, you'll find a bar or two that's open in the morning, right?
But it's right after all that commotion...
Then a can of beer will do. Having a drink outside in the breeze is a perfectly good celebration in itself.
I couldn't help but laugh at Revy's half-joking, half-serious quip.
Exchanging this kind of banter, we stepped out into the morning streets.
